ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended, Yuhan Hoesa Articles 287-2 through 287-41); Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; and the Financial Services Commission/KoFIU Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Owner Identification Regulations. No public UBO register exists; UBO identification is reported to Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and accessible to competent government authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Yuhan Hoesa Certificate of Registered Corporate Details)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: Korean notarization then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Non-Hague destination path: Korean notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization certificate, then consular legalization by the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul. The two paths are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean tax clearance certificate and corporate registry standing extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service and Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: Korean notarization of both instruments then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Non-Hague destination path: Korean notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization certificate, then destination consular legalization in Seoul. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors and Representative Director of Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize signed resolution and PoA before a Korean notary, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. For a non-Apostille state, use consular legalization through the destination state's embassy/consulate in Seoul after MOFA legalization; do not combine with Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Articles of Incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators/Shareholders of Yuhan Hoesa with Korean notary attestation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarization and Apostille. Non-Hague destination path: notarization, MOFA legalization, destination consular legalization. Use only one authentication route depending on the destination state.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended and consolidated; Yuhan Hoesa provisions), Articles 169, 288, 543, 544, 546 and 560, together with the Commercial Registration Regulations, Part 2 on corporation registration; the Registration Fees Act and the National Tax Service Framework Act apply as procedural law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Local District Court Registry, Supreme Court of Korea; jurisdictional registry determined by the registered office address
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Company Incorporation (Registration of Establishment of a Yuhan Hoesa), accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation and issuance certificate for the registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act. The Articles of Incorporation may fix any capital amount. Nevertheless, before a company registration is accepted, the entire subscribed capital must be paid in full and evidenced. Cash contributions must be deposited into a Korean Banking Business Act licensed bank or securities company, which issues a contribution payment certificate (paid-in capital deposit certificate). This certificate is the proof required by the court; it operates as a restricted/escrow verification because funds remain traceable from the account of the incorporator into the contributed capital ledger. In-kind contributions require an independent appraiser's report if not a listed security. For a corporate-registration fee illustration, a capital of KRW 10,000,000 (about USD 7,500) yields registration tax and education surcharge of roughly KRW 48,000 (about USD 36), plus court fixed fees, totaling about USD 72; the actual amount is computed by the registry on the declared capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1-2025 OF THE MEMBERS AND FIRST BOARD OF MANAGEMENT OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) — 1. INCORPORATION AND CAPITAL: RESOLVED, that the undersigned incorporators and the first manager hereby organize Yuhan Hoesa as a limited liability company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and that the Articles of Incorporation presented to this meeting are adopted without modification. 2. SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the total subscribed capital as stated in Article 6 of the Articles is accepted and that the subscription list is ratified. The manager is directed to procure full payment of each contribution in cash or through an in-kind appraiser report before filing, and to present the bank certificate of contribution payment to the District Court registry. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at the address stated in the Articles and maintained by the general manager. The manager is authorized to execute or approve leases, landlord consents, and corporate seat designations, and to file the office designation notice in the registry. 4. OFFICERS: RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are appointed: one or more representative managers, each with authority to manage ordinary business and to represent the Company in court and before state authorities, and, if required by the Articles or by the members, an auditor; the corporate seal shall be affixed by the representative manager or a designated seal custodian. Each appointed officer accepts the duties of good faith and care under the Commercial Act. 5. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the primary settlement and foreign exchange bank, as identified in the banking materials, is designated as the Company bank. The representative manager is authorized to open domestic and foreign currency accounts, sign customer agreements, apply for corporate cards, contract for SWIFT messaging, and arrange letter-of-credit issuing lines for supplier payments in dry-bulk sulfur trade. 6. FILINGS: RESOLVED, that the manager shall file the company registration, business registration, and all third-party permissions, pay fees, receive certificates, and take all steps necessary to complete the statutory formation. 7. GENERAL: RESOLVED, that all acts performed thus far in connection with formation are ratified and that this resolution shall be effective as of the date of the company registration and shall continue in full force until formally amended by the members. ADOPTED this ___ day of ______, by unanimous written consent of all members and the first manager.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Certified Korean notary public under the Notary Act of the Republic of Korea; for foreign shareholders, a Korean consular or court-authenticated power of attorney may first be necessary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Articles must be written in Korean and must state the legal form (Yuhan Hoesa), the business purpose that includes wholesale of industrial minerals, commodity brokerage, and dry-bulk cargo arrangement, the registered office location, the total subscribed capital, the method of contribution payment, and the appointment provisions for representative managers. The incorporators must appear before the notary with original identification or a certified copy of corporate registration extract for a corporate member. For non-resident members, unless already authenticated abroad, the power of attorney must bear apostille or consular legalization and be accompanied by a certified Korean translation. The notary will verify the identity, consent and legal capacity of each signatory and certify the final Articles. All pages must be sealed or initialed and the notary certificate attached.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation signed by all incorporators
Passport or national ID card of each individual incorporator
Certificate of Registration or corporate extract of any corporate incorporator
Apostilled or consularized power of attorney and certified Korean translation when an agent signs
Seal or signature specimen of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a refusal or a request for correction, the company shall correct the defective article provision or produce the missing apostille/certified translation and re-submit the document at the same notary office within one business day. If the notary requires additional verification of the registered office, a preliminary lease abstract or a written landlord consent can be submitted as a cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Full Payment of Subscribed Capital and Procurement of Contribution Payment Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bank licensed under the Korean Banking Act or a licensed securities company; for foreign-currency contributions, an authorized foreign exchange bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certified Articles are delivered, the incorporators shall open a provisional contribution deposit account in the name of the company being organized or in a designated statutorily permitted collection account. Each member must transfer the full amount of their subscribed contribution in cash, or file an in-kind appraiser report where contribution in kind is agreed. The depositary bank shall verify the identity of the payer, the source of funds for compliance with the Financial Information and Confidentiality Act, and shall issue a certificate of payment of contribution stating the payer, amount, date, and purpose. The representative manager shall preserve the original certificate for submission to the registry. No withdrawal is permitted before registration except under statutory exceptions, thus providing escrow-like protection.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of the notarized Articles of Incorporation
Identification and anti-money-laundering information of each payer
Corporate authorization of the sole member or resolution of the members
Deposit slips or electronic transfer records for every contribution
Independent appraisal report where contributions are made in kind
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the bank rejects the deposit due to AML/KYC doubts, the incorporator shall submit source-of-wealth explanations, bank references, and underlying commercial contracts for the sulfur mineral trade. If the rejection concerns the unregistered company's name, the incorporators shall use the exact preliminary articles name and present a certificate of commerce name availability issued by the competent court, if available, or open in a different licensed bank and evidence legal capacity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration with the Local District Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office address of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period following the formation decisions, the representative manager or a duly appointed registration agent shall file the Registration of Establishment application with the commercial registry. The application must identify the company, list the representative managers, the registered office, the total capital, the method of contribution and state that all contributions have been paid. In support of this statement, the registry requires original or certified copies of the notarized Articles, the bank contribution payment certificate or appraisal report, the registered office consent, and the officer appointment consents. The filing officer will examine the legality of the Articles against the Korean Commercial Act and the Uniform Commercial Registration Rules, collect the registration tax and education surcharge, and if satisfied, issue the Certificate of Company Registration and the corporate registration extract. The company comes into existence as a legal person upon entry in the registry.
required_dossiers: Complete Application for Registration of Establishment of a Yuhan Hoesa
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Contribution payment certificate from the bank or an in-kind appraisal report
Consent of the owner of the registered office or a lease agreement and certified copy of the building registry
Consent and written acceptance of each representative manager and auditor
Power of attorney for the registration agent
Receipt or payment voucher for the registration tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order (bujeong), the applicant must file a written response with the registry within the order period, usually two weeks, attaching the omitted document and paying the supplementary fee. If the registry refuses registration, the remaining applicants may file an appeal to the district court within seven days, or reconstruct the filing with corrected Articles; if the defect concerns legal capacity or capital payment, the contribution must be redeposited or the Articles amended before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration, the representative manager must file an Application for Business Registration with the local tax office within 20 days of opening the business. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate (Saupja Registration Certificate) and assign a corporate tax registration number, with VAT registration if turnover is anticipated. The application form must describe the business as wholesale trading of mineral commodities and maritime brokerage, and must identify the newly registered company, its registered office, the representative manager, and the business commencement date. The tax official may inspect the office to confirm physical presence. During this step the company should also obtain the business permit card, select an issuing tax office for e-invoices, and establish payroll and corporate tax filing accounts. The business registration number becomes the key identifier for customs, banks, and counterparties.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Company Registration and corporate registration extract
Court-issued corporate seal certificate
Application for Business Registration signed by the representative manager
Lease agreement or ownership deed and registered-office consent
Identification and copy of alien registration or passport for the representative manager
Documents showing the commencement date and business place
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office withholds registration because of incomplete evidence of the business office or director identification, the applicant may cure by filing a supplementary lease abstract, alien registration card, or a revised application. If the tax office issues an estimate or correction, the applicant may request re-examination through the local tax office and, if needed, apply for an adjudication to the National Tax Service within 30 days of the requested correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Trade Report, Customs Registration, and Bank Trade-Currency Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Customs Service (headquarters or customs with jurisdiction over the registered office); authorized foreign exchange bank for the SWIFT letter-of-credit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the Company will trade granular elemental sulfur as an industrial mineral, the representative manager must report the import/export business to the Korea Customs Service under the Foreign Trade Act, or obtain the equivalent trade business filing number, unless the transactions are only brokerage services without title transfer. The customs report requires the business registration certificate, the company registration certificate, the corporate seal certificate, and a description of the foreign trade commodity. The manager also files a customs clearance user registration and opens a bonded or foreign exchange current account with an authorized bank. For payments, the manager shall sign the bank's trade finance and anti-money-laundering agreements, and where the Founding contract requires a documentary credit, shall apply for a SWIFT-backed letter of credit or letter-of-credit confirmation line before executing the first cargo contract. No physical manufacturing or warehousing permit arises at this stage; the company shall additionally confirm with the counterparties that the ocean vessel and loading terminal hold the relevant International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea and International Maritime Dangerous Goods certificates.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate and business registration number
Company registration certificate and seal certificate
Copy of the representative manager's identification
Foreign trade report form prescribed by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and Korea Customs Service
Pro-forma sales/purchase or charter confirmation covering granular sulfur ISIC 4669 commodity description
Bank application for foreign exchange account, SWIFT and LC facility
Beneficial ownership declaration for corporate bank account due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the customs report is rejected for commodity classification or for incomplete trade status evidence, the company shall amend the HS code and the contract description and resubmit through the customs electronic clearance system. If the bank declines to open an LC because the company has no trade history, the company shall supply three-way service contracts, supplier references, and an alternative bank guarantee; if still declined, the company may apply to another authorized bank with a non-resident director signature or post a cash deposit as a performance collateral.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for the pure trading and maritime brokerage scope; if, however, the Company later operates a warehouse or cargo terminal, jurisdiction transfers to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy for industrial site licensing and to the local municipality for construction and storage permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; no manufacturing, chemical conversion, ore beneficiation, assembly, or warehousing facility is established under ISIC 4669. The required registration is the Business Registration Certificate plus the Foreign Trade report described in the SOP. Should the Company at a future stage store sulfur on its own account, the appropriate permit would be the Hazardous Substances Storage License or an industrial warehouse license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea / Korea Environment Corporation — No EIA mandate for pure wholesale brokerage and office-based operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category V Not Applicable. No land disturbance, construction, discharge, or process unit is present, and therefore no scoping or full environmental impact assessment is required. A separate site-flux EIA would be required only when loading terminals or storage tank capacity is acquired.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — zero process wastewater, zero VOC point-source emissions, and zero hazardous waste generated by the registered office and trade brokerage activities. For any future sulfur storage, the company would need to comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act and Water Environment Conservation Act, including a discharge notice for stormwater runoff and sulfur dust control to not exceed 5 mg/m3 of suspended particulate matter at the fence line.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable — there is no plant or warehouse requiring fire safety construction approval under the Act on Fire Prevention and Safety. As a minimum, the leased office must have a fire safety certificate issued by the local fire department and evacuation signage, and the Company must file a workplace basic health and safety registration under the Occupational Safety and Health Act if any employee works at the office. When vessels are engaged, the ocean carrier must hold SOLAS, International Maritime Dangerous Goods, and a valid Port State control certificate for bulk sulfur cargo, and the broker shall not charter a vessel without those certificates.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic tax portal; customs export control and clearance supervision are exercised by Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Yuhan Hoesa LLC, as a Korean domestic limited liability company, must apply for a business operator registration number through the NTS HomeTax system or its competent district tax office. The application must be submitted within 20 days after the commencement of VAT-taxable business activity. The registration dossier includes the certificate of incorporation, certificate of registered matters from the Korean registry, articles of incorporation, foreign shareholder identification documents, proof of capital where applicable, address proof for the domestic place of business, and appointment of a domestic tax representative if required by the non-resident shareholder structure. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean domestic establishment that nonetheless imports goods or supplies Korean VAT-taxable services, the NTS issues a separate non-resident business operator number after a domestic tax representative is appointed; that representative files VAT returns, issues tax invoices, and pays VAT on behalf of the non-resident. The same 10-digit business operator number is the statutory TIN, VAT ID, and withholding-agent registration number, and is electronically verified via the HomeTax portal and the UNI-PASS customs clearance network.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not operate a check-the-box regime. The Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax under the Corporate Tax Act and cannot elect pass-through treatment. The only elections available are ordinary procedural tax elections, such as election of a fiscal year and the consolidated taxation election for wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries; no hybrid mismatch election is recognized in the domestic VAT and corporate tax framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary VAT registration threshold applies to a corporation in South Korea; VAT registration is mandatory upon the commencement of taxable supplies of goods or services. The simplified VAT rules for small businesses are available only to individual business operators and do not apply to Yuhan Hoesa LLC, which must therefore register before the first export transaction, irrespective of expected turnover in KRW.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Korean VAT taxable businesses must issue tax invoices and report the invoice data to the NTS through HomeTax. Legal entities are mandatorily required to issue electronic tax invoices (e-invoices) through the HomeTax system and transmit each e-invoice to the NTS no later than the day after issuance. Individual taxpayers fall under the mandatory e-invoicing requirement when prior-year revenue exceeds the statutory threshold of KRW 100,000,000, but a limited liability company is always subject to the electronic invoicing mandate. ERP and accounting platforms issuing Korean VAT e-invoices must integrate with the National Tax Service HomeTax e-invoice API using the standard XML request/response schema. Credit-card sales, cash-receipt transactions, and point-of-sale data are transmitted to the NTS in real time through licensed VAN networks. Korea does not use a physical fiscal seal or mechanical invoice-stamping device; anti-fraud substantiation is achieved through real-time digital matching of HomeTax e-invoices, credit-card and cash-receipt data, bank foreign-exchange settlement records, UNI-PASS export declarations, and international trade statistics.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods delivered to a place outside Korea are eligible for the 0% VAT rate when the exporter files a valid export declaration with Korea Customs Service and the goods are physically removed from Korea to a foreign destination. For the dry bulk granular sulfur ore trading model, Yuhan Hoesa must demonstrate that title and risk passed to the foreign buyer, that the ore was loaded and shipped from a Korean seaport under a marine bill of lading, that the sales contract contains a clear export destination, and that the foreign exchange proceeds are received through a Korean licensed foreign-exchange bank. Export brokerage and freight-arrangement services separately contracted in respect of the export may also qualify as zero-rated export services, whereas domestic inland freight, warehousing, and port handling are standard-rated Korean VAT supplies. The zero-rated export schedule is supported by the quarterly VAT return, and an export VAT refund of attributable input VAT may be claimed when input VAT exceeds output VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: UNI-PASS Export Declaration issued by Korea Customs Service evidencing export clearance of the granular sulfur ore shipment
Marine or combined transport Bill of Lading naming the foreign buyer as consignee or notify party and confirming shipment from a Korean port to a destination outside Korea
Original commercial invoice and detailed packing list matching the customs declaration in product description, gross/net weight, packaging, and contract value

Foreign exchange settlement certificate or electronic foreign-exchange transaction record issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank evidencing actual receipt of the USD proceeds within the statutory collection period
Signed export sales contract / purchase order and an independent pre-shipment surveyor certificate confirming sulfur content, moisture, weight, and quality
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly scrutinize export zero-rating claims by cross-matching UNI-PASS export declarations, HomeTax e-invoices, marine bills of lading, vessel movement records, foreign-exchange settlement reports, and buyer payment accounts. If the documentary bundle is incomplete, inconsistent, or the goods are found not to have been physically exported, the NTS retroactively revokes the 0% rate and assesses VAT at 10% on the full export invoice value, together with penalty tax and statutory interest under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. Deliberate submission of forged export documents or false zero-rated refund claims constitutes tax evasion and may be referred to prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, exposing the entity and responsible officers to criminal fines and imprisonment, while the limitation period for tax collection on fraudulent evasion is extended to 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Investment Review Council under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberal but closely monitored foreign exchange regime. The Korean won is fully convertible for current-account transactions such as trade settlement, service payments, dividends, and royalties, provided that a domestic foreign-exchange bank receives the required declaration or report under Article 6 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital-account transactions are generally subject to a positive-list system that requires prior or ex post reporting, registration, or licensing depending on the nature of the transaction; inflows such as equity subscription proceeds require a foreign investment report, while loan drawdowns require a loan agreement registration and, when applicable, separate BOK/MOEF approval. Export proceeds are not confiscated or forcibly converted, but they must be received into a domestic foreign-exchange bank account within the statutory timeline of one year from the export date unless a written extension is granted by the foreign exchange bank; the exporter may retain the proceeds in a foreign-currency account and convert into KRW when required. Profit remittance hurdles are moderate: a foreign-invested company may remit offshore dividends upon completing the statutory audit, proving tax reconciliation, and presenting the foreign-investment registration certificate and distribution resolution; the remittance is subject to transaction purpose-code filings. Withholding tax of up to 20 per cent applies unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty, and the bank will require certificate-of-residence documentation. Although there is no blanket surrender requirement, banks apply stringent anti-money-laundering and source-of-funds checks on every conversion, and Financial Action Task Force standards are enforced by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. Overall, the won is convertible for genuine trade and investment purposes, but treasury management must route all settlement activity through regulated onshore banking channels to avoid unapproved currency swaps or unlicensed offshore settlement constructs.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations, resident exporters must collect export proceeds within one year from the export declaration date unless a written extension is approved by an authorized foreign-exchange bank for justifiable causes such as extended payment terms or deferred collection; the proceeds must be received in a foreign-currency account at an authorized domestic bank or sold promptly to an authorized foreign-exchange bank, and the onshore receipt must be reported using the standard export-receipt code in the bank's electronic system. No compulsory percentage conversion into KRW is mandated; the exporter may retain 100 per cent of the foreign-currency receipts in a foreign-currency account, but any conversion to KRW must be documented with the matching export customs declaration and commercial invoice.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW plus USD/EUR/CNY multi-currency)
Capital Escrow Account and Domestic Trade Settlement Account
Foreign-Exchange Trading Account and Export Proceeds Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-nil for a Korean-domiciled operating entity. Overseas digital EMI platforms such as Revolut Business, Airwallex, and Wise generally lack a domestic foreign-exchange bank license under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and therefore cannot lawfully maintain full KRW settlement, issue Korean disbursement instructions, or act as the primary settlement bank for export-receipt collection. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa must route cross-border payments, LC issuance, and foreign-currency balances through an authorized domestic bank or a licensed domestic electronic-financial-transaction provider holding BOK/MOEF registrations. An EMI can be used only as a supplementary remittance channel for minor, pre-approved low-value disbursements, and even then only if the EMI holds a foreign-exchange business registration with the Bank of Korea and the customer passes the onshore bank's reimbursement and AML controls. In practice, compliance officers will reject an EMI as the main treasury channel, and counterparties in the sulfur bulk trade will refuse to accept letters of credit issued by an unlicensed platform.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for at least one statutory representative, normally the CEO or a designated director, at the time of initial corporate account activation at major domestic banks. The designated signatory must appear in person at the branch with the original corporate registration certificate issued by the National Tax Service, the Yuhan Hoesa articles of incorporation, the certificate of entity existence, and a passport or equivalent national ID. Korean banks do not, as a general rule, accept a remote consular proxy opening for the initial KYC interview where the representative is a foreign national; some banks permit a power of attorney for document submission, but the biometric and financial-risk interview must be conducted in person before an account officer. If the CEO is overseas, a court-certified or consular-notarized power of attorney may authorize an in-country officer to file paperwork, but the authorized officer must still attend a branch interview with proper identification and documentary evidence of authority. The bank will also complete beneficial-ownership verification under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and the core AML regulation, which normally requires the UBO's date of birth, citizenship, passport copies, a signed source-of-funds declaration, and a statement concerning politically exposed persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or layered ultimate beneficial ownership where the shareholder is a foreign holding company, trust, or nominee rather than a natural-person Korean resident director.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the company charter, shareholder register, share transfer ledgers, and a notarized UBO certificate reflecting every natural person owning 25 per cent or more of the LLC; include current passports of all UBOs, recent foreign-jurisdiction corporate registry extracts dated within three months, a written confirmation of the ultimate business rationale, and a signed declaration confirming that no politically exposed person or sanctioned entity is concealed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-profile mismatch involving a newly formed LLC with no historical financials but expected to move high-value bulk sulfur shipments through multiple counterparties, vessel charters, and freight intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver executed master purchase and sales contracts for each planned trade, commercial invoices, packing lists, a written logistics schedule with vessel name and draft Bill of Lading, port terminal storage receipts, a market-value price opinion from a recognized commodity index such as Argus sulfur, and an independent third-party quality assay of elemental sulfur to demonstrate arm's-length invoicing and no over- or under-invoicing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and restricted-party red flags in counterparty, freight, or insurance documentation where shipments transit through or sell into jurisdictions that may be under international sanctions, especially when the charterer uses unvetted flags or shell intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce negative media and sanctions screening reports for all legal entities and UBOs, vessel screening based on IMO number and clean voyage history from reputable maritime data providers, freighter confirmation that the vessel and cargo will not call at OFAC, UN, or EU-listed ports, a full marine cargo insurance certificate, and an undertaking that payment proceeds will be remitted only to title-verified counterparty bank accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth and funding origin questions where capital will be contributed by non-resident investors through overseas banks into the Korean LLC, creating concerns over currency smuggling, trade-based money laundering, or unlicensed money remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit six months of bank statements from each contributing investor, the signed capital contribution resolution, confirmation of the foreign-investment reporting receipt from the foreign-exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, tax and compliance certificates from the contributor's home jurisdiction, and a notarized source-of-wealth declaration containing a description of business revenues, real-estate disposal proceeds, or listed-asset liquidation events.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign investment into the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must comply with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA). The non-resident investor opens a temporary foreign-currency receipt account at an authorized domestic foreign-exchange bank, wires the USD, EUR, or CNY capital under the correct SWIFT purpose code for inward foreign investment, and files the required foreign-investment report with the Bank of Korea or Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), either before or simultaneously with the share subscription. After the report is accepted, the bank issues a foreign-investment registration certificate and the funds are converted into KRW at the onshore market rate; conversion is settled against the foreign-investment report and certificate. Although no custodial capital escrow account is statutorily mandated, most banks hold the initial subscription in a segregated non-interest-bearing account until the share subscription is executed and the business registration is filed. The capital verification for treasury and accounting purposes is evidenced by the foreign-investment registration certificate, the remittance SWIFT MT103 showing the investor as remitter, the foreign-exchange contract rate and confirmation, and the board resolution approving the subscription.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the bulk dry-shipping and brokerage activity, outbound settlements should be executed through onshore clearing rails only. First, for advance payments to foreign suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 from the Korean bank account to the receiving bank, annotating the transfer with the true BOK trade purpose code and attaching the commercial contract and customs declaration in the bank transfer file. Second, for documentary shipments, issue an Irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit through the opening Korean bank in the exporter's favour, with the bank advising through a first-class correspondent; this is the preferred rail for high-value elemental sulfur cargoes because it conditions payment on presentation of on-board Bills of Lading, quality certificates, and invoices. Third, for open-account or collections flows, use Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A), under which the Korean bank forwards title documents to the collecting bank and releases documents against sight payment or acceptance; this is permissible for lower-value or repeated broker flows but carries payment risk. The Korean entity may also make KRW vendor payments to domestic freight and handling partners, while foreign-currency payments must be reported in the bank's foreign-exchange transaction system and the bank will retain a full cash-flow audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/KRW deliverable forwards are permitted only when there is a genuine current- or capital-account performance obligation; the bank requires a signed underlying trade contract and proof of export or import exposure to support the hedge.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) trades are allowed only for documented trade exposure via a bank licensed to operate the onshore NDF market; resident entities are expected to use deliverable forwards, and speculative offshore NDF leverage should be avoided because it violates the anti-speculation principle.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps are permissible for hedging medium-term foreign-currency loan principal and interest exposures when the underlying borrowing has been registered with the authorities and the swap is executed with an authorized bank or licensed broker.

Domestic FX option strategies such as purchased USD/KRW calls or puts are permissible for trade hedging, subject to the same real-demand documentation rule; uncovered option selling is not permitted for standalone profit generation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return and Financial Statement Submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the close of the prior fiscal year (December 31); fiscal year end can be changed with NTS approval, and if so, the deadline is the last day of the third month after the new fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 0.7% of unpaid tax per day up to 365 days, neglect penalty up to 20% of unpaid tax, false filing penalty up to 40% of understated tax; continued failure to file for three consecutive years triggers compulsory collection and administrative disposition of corporate closure or strike-off of the entity from the commercial registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Submission to the External Audit and Supervision System (EASS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) via the External Audit and Supervision System (EASS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 weeks after the annual statutory shareholders' meeting, which must be held within 6 months after the fiscal year end (on or before June 30 following the fiscal year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the audit report to EASS results in administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,700); repeated negligence may trigger a formal investigation by the FSS Securities and Futures Commission, referral for criminal prosecution, and suspension or revocation of the entity's business license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report Filing and Financial Statement Disclosure at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Court of Korean Commercial Registry (Registration Court) under the Supreme Court Administration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year end (on or before June 30 following the fiscal year end); requires resolution by the annual general meeting of members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of KRW 1,000,000 (approximately USD 740) for overdue registration; continued non-registration for more than 1 year after the deadline is an explicit trigger for ex officio strike-off and ultimate dissolution of the entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding Tax and Social Insurance Annual Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Employment Insurance Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 10 following the fiscal year end for withholding tax annual reconciliation; February 10 for prior-year withholding certificate submission for employees and resident directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 10% of the unreported withheld amount, 0.7% per day late payment surcharge, and criminal referral from NTS for intentional non-payment; insurance contributions unpaid for 3 consecutive months triggers compulsory collection and business suspension orders

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Exchange Transaction Report for Cross-Border Trade Settlements (LC / Swift transactions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bank of Korea and Korea Customs Service via mandatory foreign exchange bank reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the end of each quarter for direct investment and trade settlement reporting; annual report filed by January 31 following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of up to KRW 100,000,000 (approximately USD 74,000) for unregistered cross-border transactions, mandatory delay or refusal of future trade settlement processing by the FX bank, and a freeze on foreign currency bank accounts; repeated violations trigger criminal referral and revocation of the trade license under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Mining and Mineral Trade Annual Business Report (for sulfur ore bulk trading)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Customs Service and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: June 30 following the fiscal year end; also requires real-time import/export declaration through UNI-PASS for every cargo shipment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 30,000,000 (approximately USD 22,000), revocation of customs broker license, mandatory inspection of all future cargoes, and forfeiture of export promotion benefits; failure to report two consecutive years triggers criminal investigation for revenue loss

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Juridical Entities, mandatory independent CPA audit is triggered if any one of the following applies: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million); (b) total revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million); (c) the entity has 30 or more employees on average; (d) the entity is a LL C with 10 or more members; (e) the entity has outstanding bonds or securities listed on a public exchange; (f) the sovereign debt rating is assigned or the entity falls within a regulated financial industry; (g) the entity exceeds KRW 7 billion (approximately USD 5.2 million) in assets and KRW 5 billion (approximately USD 3.7 million) in revenue simultaneously for two consecutive years; (h) the entity receives government subsidies or is a public-interest entity. Once any threshold is crossed, the audit must be performed by a licensed Korean CPA firm registered with the FSS, and the audit report must be filed on the External Audit and Supervision System (EASS).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as adopted by the Republic of Korea and fully converged with IFRS, mandatory for all publicly listed entities and entities meeting the audit thresholds; entities below the K-IFRS mandatory scope may apply Korea Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Korean GAAP) for non-listed entities, or Korea SME Accounting Standards (K-SMES) for small and medium-size entities with assets under KRW 7 billion and revenue under KRW 5 billion. All accounting books must be kept on the accrual basis in Korean won.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Commercial Act and the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, every Yuhan Hoesa must maintain an up-to-date register of ultimate beneficial owners. An annual confirmation is due with the regular general meeting, where each member or shareholder must declare the ultimate beneficial owner. Any share transfer, change in beneficial ownership, or change in the register of members must be registered with the Korean Commercial Registry within 30 days of the change, and must also be reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit reporting portal. For any share transfer achieving 10% or more ownership, a special confirmation is required within 30 days. A nominee or shell structure is prohibited; failure to disclose a UBO triggers a criminal penalty of up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 37,000) or imprisonment up to 5 years.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Typical annual fee range: USD 150 to USD 350
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Typical certified audit fee range: USD 6,500 to USD 18,000 for an entity under the mandatory audit threshold but preparing audited financial statements to support trade finance lines of credit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.5% top combined corporate income tax rate (25% national corporate tax plus 2.5% local income tax surcharge, computed as 10% of the 25% national CIT); lower progressive national rates of 9% on up to KRW 200 million and 19% on the KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion tranche apply with an equivalent 10% local surcharge
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic trading-sector free-zone holiday for sulfur mineral ore trading; available statutory reliefs include R&D tax credits up to 50% for eligible technology investments, foreign-investor incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Free Economic Zone tax breaks, facility and employment tax credits, foreign tax credit relief for Korean-sourced cross-border income, and ordinary deductions for bad debts, depreciation and documented overseas marketing costs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (CIT Form 1) together with the supplementary International Transactions Annex, electronically filed by the company's tax agent through the Korean National Tax Service (NTS) 'Hometax' portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end the filing deadline is 31 March of the following year; an extension of up to one month may be granted by the NTS on application, with longer extensions available for overseas audit or disaster circumstances

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identification and Foreign Shareholder Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, business registration number, registered office, representative director, industrial classification code, and a schedule of all shareholders identifying each non-resident shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident shareholder of Yuhan Hoesa LLC, disclose the overseas tax identification number, country of residence, beneficial owner, shareholding percentage, and foreign address; this schedule is matched by the NTS with dividend withholding payments and DTA claims, and any misstatement exposes the company to an assessment and penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Tax Base: Gross Income and Deductible Expense Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before tax arising from brokerage commissions, dry bulk marine freight, granular elemental sulfur sales, letter of credit discount income, and financial revenue, reduced by deductible operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean resident LLC is subject to Korean corporate income tax on its worldwide income; expenses paid to foreign related parties for management, charter hire, or service fees are deductible only if there is a written contract, actual service performance, and economic substance; non-arm's-length amounts must be adjusted in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable Income Adjustments and Transfer Pricing Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income, including add-backs of disallowed expenses, exclusions for tax-exempt income, carryforward loss offsets, and transfer pricing adjustments on cross-border related-party transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the International Transactions Annex and state every transaction with overseas affiliates; if the statutory Korean turnover and related-party transaction thresholds are exceeded for Local File or Master File, those documents must be attached or available; the adopted arm's-length method and comparability analysis must be stated to avoid a transfer pricing audit adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax Credits, Incentives, and Prior-Year Loss Deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate tax after foreign tax credits, domestic tax credits, deduction of tax-exempt income, and application of carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prior-year operating losses may be carried forward for 10 years; foreign tax credits are capped by the Korean tax attributable to the same foreign-source income; tax credits or losses of Yuhan Hoesa LLC cannot be passed through to non-resident shareholders, and any reduced treaty withholding on shareholder dividends is reported through the withholding schedule, not in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Final Tax Payable and Advance Payment Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed final corporate income tax liability after intermediate prepayments, including the balance payable or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company previously reported low taxable income or omitted freight and brokerage commissions, the NTS will impose an understatement penalty of 10% of the omitted tax, rising to 40% where the omission is fraudulent; the foreign parent's financing of the balance through shareholder loans must be documented to prevent deemed dividend characterization.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the CIT return by the statutory deadline triggers a late-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax, increasing to 40% where concealment or fraud is found; non-negligent underreporting carries a 10% surtax on the understated tax while gross negligence or fraud carries 20% or 40%; unpaid tax bears a late-payment surcharge of 0.022% per day for a maximum of 36 months; serious failures lead to NTS blacklisting of the company and its director, travel restrictions, asset sealing, and referral to the public prosecutor for criminal tax evasion proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory outbound dividend withholding is 20% on the gross dividend plus a 2% local income tax surcharge (computed as 10% of the 20% national withholding), producing a total 22% rate for dividends paid by Yuhan Hoesa LLC to a non-resident shareholder; this is subject to reduction or exemption under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the foreign shareholder must (i) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its resident-country tax authority and provide it to the Korean withholding agent; (ii) submit the Korean NTS reduced-rate withholding application, official 'Application for Non-Taxation or Reduced Taxation of Foreign Investor', before remittance or as part of the refund process; (iii) provide a beneficial-ownership declaration confirming the recipient is the true owner, has no obligation to pass the income on to another person, and is not a shell or conduit entity; (iv) supply documents proving, where the treaty requires it, a minimum shareholding period and voting rights threshold for the lower dividend rate; (v) keep all documentation for at least five years after remittance; if the reduced rate is not applied at the time of payment, the excess withholding may be reclaimed through the NTS refund procedure with statutory interest from the date following overpayment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest paid to non-residents are each subject to a statutory withholding rate of 20% plus a 2% local income tax surcharge, totaling 22%; under most Korean DTAs, including the Korea-US treaty, royalty and interest withholding is commonly reduced to 10%, and in some treaties interest is 0% for export-like credit arrangements or certain government-backed loans; reduced treaty rates are available only when the payee is the beneficial owner and the complete DTA relief protocol has been satisfied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File documentation become compulsory when the Korean company's annual turnover equals or exceeds KRW 100 billion and total cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 50 billion; a simplified International Transactions Annex is also required in the corporate tax return when transactions with a single foreign related party exceed KRW 5 billion, and a Country-by-Country Report is required when the consolidated group revenue reaches KRW 1.5 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the NTS applies the substance-over-form doctrine and anti-fragmentation rules under the Framework Act on National Taxes; a Yuhan Hoesa LLC that has real board meetings, experienced sulfur-trading and freight staff, independent decision-making on chartering and sales, substantive bank mandates, and risk-bearing capacity is treated as a Korean resident company; where treaty shopping is suspected, the foreign parent must prove that the Korean LLC is not a conduit and that its Core Income-Generating Activities, including negotiation, inspection, logistics direction, and assumption of cargo price and shipping risk, are genuinely performed in Korea; failure to demonstrate substance will result in treaty benefit denial and re-characterization of payments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean director knowingly omits brokerage commissions, freight charter income, and sulfur ore resale profits from the corporate income tax return; diverts revenues into offshore bank accounts; or pays fabricated management fees, service fees, charter hire, or royalties to a foreign parent to strip taxable profit without any actual service or economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korean tax evasion law, in particular the fraudulent-evasion offense under the Act on the Punishment of Tax Evaders, provides imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 200 million, with additional administrative penalties of 40% of the understated tax and daily late-payment surcharges; the NTS is empowered to redetermine the taxable base for six years in fraud cases and to enforce collection through seizure of corporate and personal assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced when a director personally directed the concealment; the director becomes secondarily liable for the unpaid corporate tax under the National Tax Collection Act, may be blacklisted and placed on the NTS overseas-travel restriction list until the tax is paid, can have personal bank accounts and real estate attached, and may be criminally convicted to imprisonment; civil restitution to damaged creditors and the tax authority is also ordered by Korean courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Conduit Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Yuhan Hoesa LLC is maintained as a paper entity with no physical office, employees, operating assets, or logistics contracts in Korea; all substantive purchase and resale decisions, cargo chartering instructions, and risk decisions are made by the foreign parent in another jurisdiction; profits are immediately repatriated as service fees or royalties in a structure designed solely to access Korean DTA reductions on dividends, interest, or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will disregard or re-characterize the intermediary company under the substance-over-form doctrine embedded in the Framework Act on National Taxes and may apply the Principal Purpose Test contained in Korea's tax treaties; denied expense deductions will be restored to taxable income, outbound payments will be re-tolled as dividends subject to 22% withholding, and a penalty of 40% of the false documentation or understatement may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false board minutes, substance certificates, or treaty-relief applications can be held personally and jointly liable for all additional corporate taxes, interest, and penalties; they face asset forfeiture, travel bans, and blacklisting by the NTS; if they knowingly cause abuse of a tax treaty, they are exposed to criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion, with imprisonment terms of up to 3 years under Korean tax-coordination law, and foreign parent indemnities will not protect them from Korean personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, KYC, and Trade Sanctions Violations in International Commodity Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company processes high-value Swift and Letter of Credit payments for sulfur mineral ore cargoes without identifying beneficial owners, conducting customer due diligence, or screening counterparties, banks, freight forwarders, and ultimate consignees against United Nations sanctions and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit watchlists; payments are routed through third-country shell companies or the bill of lading and commodity invoices are intentionally misdeclared to the issuing bank or Korea Customs Service.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, violations carry imprisonment of up to 5 years and criminal fines of up to KRW 100 million; Korea Customs Service is separately authorized to impose forfeiture or penalty duties up to ten times the misdeclared value under the Customs Act, and the letter of credit may be dishonored by the Korean bank for prescribed false documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot rely on the LLC's limited liability for intentional KYC or sanctions violations; a director who signs false transfer instructions or import declarations may be prosecuted personally as a principal offender or accomplice, subjected to emergency asset-freezing orders, blacklisted by the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit, arrested abroad and extradited to Korea for trial, and ordered to compensate the bank, counterparties, and governmental bodies for losses; personal criminal imprisonment and confiscation of traced assets are available remedies.
